name: Buzhong Yiqi formula (Hochuekkito)
short: Hochuekkito (Japanese version) case reports: liver injury and hepatic encephalopathy needing plasma exchange; pleuritis. Trials: mild nausea, diarrhoea as on placebo; grade 1 impaired liver function.
text: Buzhong Yiqi (Bu Zhong Yi Qi Tang) is the same named formula as the Japanese Kampo medicine Hochuekkito, and several cited sources concern that Japanese preparation. The most serious reported harm is from a case report: a 57-year-old man developed jaundice, liver injury and hepatic encephalopathy after taking Hochuekkito for fatigue, needed intravenous steroid pulse therapy and plasma exchange, and recovered (his liver function later worsened again because of an antibiotic); the authors say the possibility of drug-induced liver injury should be taken into account. Another case report described eosinophilic pleuritis (inflammation of the lining around the lung) in a 33-year-old woman about 10 weeks after starting Hochuekkito, which improved when it was stopped. In trials, a 24-week placebo-controlled trial of Hochuekkito taken by mouth in 91 people with atopic dermatitis found only mild adverse events such as nausea and diarrhoea, in both groups without statistical difference; a randomized pilot study in 42 people with myeloproliferative neoplasms reported grade 1 impaired liver function as the only adverse event; and in a 28-day randomized trial in hospital-acquired pneumonia (168 patients analysed), no serious adverse events occurred in either group with Buzhong Yiqi decoction added to standard treatment, and 28-day deaths were 13.33% with the decoction and 21.2% without it, a difference that was not significant. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
